summary: Add durable host admission holds with owner release and explicit configured-operator recovery

replay.detail: Host holds persist independently of runs and daemon lifetimes; terminal runs and answered asks never release them.

schema.detail: An authoritative local_host_holds table stores owner, revision, reason, affected operations, originating run and receipt. Holds are not replicated launch capabilities.

rules.detail: Only the owning execution host writes holds. Release requires authenticated owner identity and an exact expected revision. Recovery requires the configured local owning person, an exact revision and a reason; bound agents/runs cannot impersonate that operator. Recovery is limited to run-owned holds with a positively terminal owning run; missing and nonterminal runs retain custody. Each mutation commits a host-hold.changed local observation in the same transaction to invalidate incremental admission.

compatibility.detail: Attention and now show active host-hold source rows; the hosts API uses native local authenticated identities rather than trusting a payload actor. Durable holds operate independently of the native resource-lane telemetry integration.

downtime.detail: No restart or migration of existing execution records is required.

manual.detail: No holds or host policies are created automatically.

recovery.detail: Use fractal hosts release HOST HOLD --expected-revision REV --resolution TEXT as the owner, or fractal hosts recover HOST HOLD --expected-revision REV --reason TEXT as the configured host operator after the owning run is positively terminal. Missing owner runs cannot be recovered. Separate host-hold.released and host-hold.recovered history facts record the acting identity, original owner, reason and revisions. Recovery preserves the original owner. Holds retain no executor capacity; terminal runs, answered asks and lease expiry never clear quarantine.
